title: The Kobayashi Metric on the Asymptotic Teichmüller Spaces
content: This paper resolves Fletcher's 2010 open problem [4] by proving the metric identification theorem: the Kobayashi pseudo-distance coincides with the asymptotic Teichmüller metric on the asymptotic Teichmüller space AT(X) of an arbitrary hyperbolic Riemann surface X. The proof rests on the holomorphic lifting theorem: every holomorphic map \( \mathbb{D}\to\mathrm{AT}(X) \) lifts holomorphically to a map \( \mathbb{D}\to T(X) \) along the canonical projection \( \Pi\colon T(X)\to\mathrm{AT}(X) \). The construction depends on three well-established facts: (I). \( \Pi \) is a holomorphic affine submersion with explicit local holomorphic sections and a canonical fibrewise translation action that is independent of the choice of local trivialisation, constructed in [3]; (II). this fibrewise translation action (see the canonical fibrewise translation action in Section 3) is holomorphic in parameters whenever the base point varies holomorphically [3]; (III). the sheaf of holomorphic sections of any holomorphic Banach vector bundle over a relatively compact bounded pseudoconvex domain in \( \mathbb{C} \) with a complete plurisubharmonic exhaustion function is cohesive and has vanishing first Čech cohomology [11, Theorem 2 and Theorem 9.1]. These facts allow local lifts to be glued into a global holomorphic lift via a standard Čech cohomology argument. Combined with the contraction property of the Kobayashi pseudo-distance under holomorphic maps and the Royden--Gardiner theorem on T(X) [6, 14], the holomorphic lifting theorem immediately implies the metric identification theorem on AT(X). The method provides a robust and completely rigorous template for lifting and intrinsic metric comparison problems on infinite-dimensional quotient complex manifolds modelled on Banach or Fréchet spaces.
